prerequisites: It is recommended to have passed or be enrolled in all subjects from courses prior to the one in which this subject is located.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the basic aspects of industrial electrical installations
Understand the basic aspects and operation of electrical protections in Low Voltage
Know the main aspects of the Low Voltage Electrotechnical Regulation and its application to industrial electrical installations
Understand the basic aspects of handling topographic instruments and their application to topographic surveys as well as re-layout operations
Know the processes of preparing topographic plans, generating profiles, and calculating volumes
Know the characteristics of basic construction elements
Acquire knowledge about management, control, monitoring, and environmental impact techniques for construction works

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of Geomatics: Fundamentals of geodesy and cartography: Geoid and ellipsoid, cartographic projections, coordinate systems. Scale. Cartographic sources. Geospatial sensors and topography: Spatial, aerial and terrestrial sensors. Topography and topographic surveys. Total stations, LiDAR, cameras, GNSS. Planimetric and altimetric methods. Digital terrain models. Use of free software to consolidate and expand theoretical knowledge.

Applications of Topography: Photogrammetry and LiDAR: Photogrammetry: Definitions. General method of photogrammetry: Camera models, lenses, coordinate systems. Extrinsic and intrinsic parameters. Parallax and base. Height measurement above terrain. Photogrammetric flight planning: Planning phases. Ground control points. Flight and trajectory parameters. Drones: Legislation and licenses for use. Introduction to LiDAR processing: Definitions and typologies. Terrestrial and aerial acquisition systems. Components. Sources of error. Applications. Point clouds: Coordinates, attributes, reading formats. Use of free software to consolidate and expand theoretical knowledge: Metashape, CloudCompare.

Geographic Information Systems: Urban Planning and Spatial Planning: Geographic Information Systems (GIS): Introduction, definitions. Components and uses. Web resources based on GIS. Geographic data. Definition and components. Data models: Layer division. Raster and vector representation models. Introduction to spatial planning and its relationship with GIS: Land uses, definition and dimensions of spatial planning. Administrative spatial planning in Spain. Legal regime of land. Urban planning. Consultations in geospatial information sources and geographic information servers. Access to urban planning and spatial planning regulations. Use of free software to consolidate and expand theoretical knowledge: QGIS.

Construction and BIM methodology: Design guidelines in building. Regulations. Introduction to energy efficiency and its technologies in construction. Introduction to BIM methodology. Definition and regulations. EN ISO 19650 and application in BIM projects. Incorporation of BIM in the public sector. Standardization, IFC model. Success cases of BIM-based projects. Concept of Scan-to-BIM. Digital twins. Examples of software for BIM methodologies. Practical example of a Scan-to-BIM process from a 3D point cloud of a building acquired with a LiDAR sensor. Elaboration of 2D plans and 3D models of the building. Use of software with student license: Autocad, Revit.
The Electrical System: The national electrical system. System subjects. System operation. Electricity market.

Components of an Electrical Installation: Conductors and cables. Switching elements. Protection elements. Control elements. Transformers. Motors. Lighting. Energy measurement systems. Power factor correction.
Design and Calculation of Electrical Installations: Starting data. Load forecasting. Calculations by admissible current. Calculations by voltage drop. Calculations by short-circuit current.

Applicable Regulations: Low Voltage Electrotechnical Regulation (REBT). High Voltage Electrical Installations Regulation (MIE-RAT). High Voltage Electrical Lines Regulation (LAT). Technical Building Code (CTE).
Electrical Diagrams: Symbology. Power diagrams. Single-line diagram. Control diagrams.
Lighting Technology: Basic concepts of lighting. Photometric magnitudes. Calculation methods.

assessment_methods.method: Practice report, practicum and external internships

assessment_rules: The final exam will consist of two sections, one corresponding to Topography and Construction, and the other to Electrical Installations content. Both parts will include theoretical questions and application exercises. Each section will be evaluated from 0 to 10 points, with the final grade obtained from the average value. A minimum of 4 points in each of the parts of each section will be necessary to pass the subject. The grade for passed practical work will be saved for the calls of the same academic year. Any unethical behavior (copying, plagiarism, unauthorized use of electronic devices, etc.) will result in a global failing grade (0.0) for the academic year.
